citation: PDB 7XJV (database-level structural support; primary citation listed as To Be Published, no PMID or DOI)
claim_tested: MNT4 retains the donor-binding residues of a characterised GT71 member
key_finding: 2.8 A Mnt2 (P53059) holo structure with Mn2+ and GDP-alpha-D-mannose bound defines 21 donor/metal contact residues; MNT4 is identical to Mnt2 at 15 of 21, including the DSD motif (D300-S301-D302) and metal ligand N481
context: S. cerevisiae Mnt2 lumenal domain, X-ray crystallography
confidence_limits: High for the Mnt2 site definition. The MNT4 mapping is sequence inference through a 43.9% identity alignment, not a MNT4 structure

citation: AlphaFold DB AF-P53745-F1 v6 and AF-P53059-F1 v6 (database-level computational support)
claim_tested: MNT4 adopts the GT-A fold with an unoccluded donor pocket
key_finding: Core superposition of the MNT4 model on 7XJV chain A gives 1.05 A RMSD over 446 of 498 matched Calpha pairs; after ligand transfer, MNT4 D302 lies 1.65 A and N481 2.20 A from the Mn2+ position, and all eight catalytic residues are within 1.91-3.83 A of GDP-mannose atoms, with no steric occlusion of the pocket
context: AlphaFold2 models, local Kabsch superposition with iterative outlier trimming
confidence_limits: Predicted structure with a transferred rather than an observed ligand. Short contacts reflect the transfer, not a refined complex

citation: This analysis (UniProt PF11051 retrieval, 67 proteins, 10 Saccharomycetaceae species)
claim_tested: MNT4's catalytic site is maintained by selection rather than decaying
key_finding: MNT4 is the fastest-drifting paralog (64.8% mean identity to sensu stricto orthologs vs 72.1-81.8% for the others) yet holds 89.3% identity at the 21 donor/metal positions, a +24.5 point excess over its own background, permutation p = 3.6e-06; all four orthologs keep the exact DSD and all three metal ligands
context: Saccharomyces sensu stricto orthologs, local Needleman-Wunsch alignment and 5000-draw permutation test
confidence_limits: Ortholog assignment by best global alignment score, not by synteny. MNT4 orthologs recovered only within Saccharomyces

citation: This analysis (zone partition of 7XJV chain A)
claim_tested: MNT4 resembles Mnt2 specifically, not just generically
key_finding: In the acceptor-proximal second shell (35 residues within 12 A of GDD C11 and beyond 4.5 A of the donor) MNT4 matches Mnt2 at 71.4% identity, +26.4 points over its own structural background, p = 0.0016. MNN1, MNN2 and MNN5 show no enrichment there (p = 0.38, 0.33, 0.28); MNT3 is intermediate (p = 0.026)
context: Mnt2 structural frame, five paralogs mapped through alignment
confidence_limits: The acceptor is not present in 7XJV, so the shell is a geometric proxy for the acceptor groove

citation: This analysis (neighbour-joining, 20 taxa, Kimura-corrected protein distances)
claim_tested: Which characterised member is MNT4 closest to
key_finding: The four MNT4 sequences form a clade sister to the MNT2 clade. Distances from Sc MNT4: MNT2 0.978, MNT3 1.592, MNN1 1.603, MNN5 2.194, MNN2 2.296. Whole-protein identity to MNT2 is 43.9%, the highest of any pair involving MNT4
confidence_limits: Distance-based tree with no bootstrap resampling. Topology at the MNT2/MNT4 split is consistent with pairwise identity but not independently supported

stance: refutes (the BP claim), qualifies (the MF claim)
claim_tested: MNT4 is required for O-linked mannan extension
key_finding: Direct statement that MNT4 (YNR059w) does not appear to be required for O-glycan synthesis, in contrast to MNT2 and MNT3
context: S. cerevisiae deletion strains, O-glycan structural analysis
confidence_limits: A single-deletion test. Redundancy with MNT2 would produce the same negative result

claim_tested: MNT4 reaches the Golgi where the family reaction occurs
key_finding: SWAT-GFP fusion localizes to the ER and the mCherry fusion to the vacuole, not the Golgi. The library places tags at the amino terminus, which is where MNT4's type II signal-anchor (residues 11-29) sits
context: S. cerevisiae high-throughput N-terminal tagging library
confidence_limits: N-terminal tagging of a signal-anchored protein is a recognised mislocalization hazard, so the result is not decisive either way

citation: UniProt P53745 and the five paralog records (database-level)
claim_tested: Is there any protein-level evidence for MNT4
key_finding: MNT4 is PE 3 (inferred from homology) while MNN1, MNT2, MNT3, MNN2 and MNN5 are all PE 1. UniProt gives MNT4 subcellular location 'Membrane' only; the other five are Golgi membrane or cis-Golgi network. SGD's protein_experiment_details endpoint returns an empty list for YNR059W
confidence_limits: Absence of evidence in curated records, not evidence of absence of the protein

citation: SGD GO annotation audit for YNR059W (23 annotations, database-level)
claim_tested: What supports the existing MNT4 GO annotations
key_finding: GO:0000033 is 3x ISS and 4x IBA; GO:0006493 is 1x IC and 4x IBA; GO:0005794 is 1x IEA and 4x IBA. The manually curated CC annotation is the root GO:0005575 with evidence code ND. No EXP, IDA, IMP, IGI or IPI annotation exists

claim_tested: Does any mnt4 phenotype point to glycosylation
key_finding: 9 records, all from genome-wide screens: viable null, decreased competitive fitness, decreased chemical resistance, increased chronological lifespan, increased invasive growth on overexpression. None is a glycosylation or cell wall mannan phenotype
context: S. cerevisiae genome-wide deletion and overexpression screens
confidence_limits: Screens are not designed to detect mannan structure changes

claim_tested: Does the published MNT4 functional literature apply to YNR059W
key_finding: The paper's CaMnt3, CaMnt4 and CaMnt5 belong to the C. albicans MNT1/KRE2 family (GT15, PF01793). CaMnt3 aligns to Sc Kre2 at 44.3% identity (score +769) and to every Sc GT71 paralog at negative global score. The only C. albicans protein UniProt names MNT4 (Q59MZ9, MNN16) is GT71, but its best Sc hit is MNT4 at only 28.2% identity with MNT3 at 24.5% and MNT2 at 24.6% behind it
context: C. albicans SC5314 null mutants; local alignment against S. cerevisiae references
confidence_limits: The alignment is conclusive for family separation. The non-orthology of Q59MZ9 to ScMnt4 is a confidence statement, not a formal orthology test
